subject: english
chapter_title: Madam Rides the Bus: Valli's First Journey

concepts.title: Valli's Favourite Pastime and the Bus Plan
concepts.definition: Valliammai, called Valli for short, is an eight-year-old with no playmates, and her favourite pastime is standing at her front door watching the street, where the sight of a new set of passengers on the bus fills her with unending joy.
concepts.key_idea: Over many days and months Valli listens carefully to conversations of neighbours and casual buyers, gathering every detail about the bus journey to town.
question_patterns: what was valli's favourite pastime
what was a source of unending joy for valli
how old was valli and what was her full name
how did valli gather information about the bus journey
why did valli watch the street so carefully
what small details about the bus did valli collect

solution_steps.explain: Valli is eight, called Valliammai, with no playmates of her own age.
Standing at the front door and watching the street was her most absorbing pastime.
She picked up details of distance, time and fare from careful listening, a few questions here and there.

concepts.title: Saving the Fare and Planning Secretly
concepts.definition: The fare was thirty paise one way, and Valli saved every coin by resisting her temptation to buy peppermints, toys, balloons and the ride on the merry-go-round, planning a bus ride without telling anyone at home.
concepts.key_idea: Sacrifice was difficult but disciplined saving made the fare possible, showing Valli's determination and self-control.
question_patterns: how did valli save up money for her first journey
what temptations did valli resist to save money
why did valli plan her journey in secret
what was the bus fare for valli's journey
why was it difficult for valli to save the fare
what does valli's saving show about her character

solution_steps.explain: Thirty paise each way, the same fare back on the same bus.
Peppermints, toys, balloons and the merry-go-round ride were all given up to collect the money.
Valli planned to slip away while the household napped, keeping the journey a secret.

concepts.title: The Bus Journey and the Laughing Cow
concepts.definition: On her first journey Valli stands on her seat to drink in the sights, laughs at a young cow galloping wildly in the middle of the road in front of the bus, and refuses to leave the bus at the station.
concepts.key_idea: The conductor's joking manner, calling her madam, amuses Valli, while her refusal to leave the bus shows her careful plan to return home on the same bus.
question_patterns: what did valli see on her way that made her laugh
why did valli refuse to look out of the window on the return journey
how did the conductor behave with valli
why didn't valli get off the bus at the bus station
describe the sights valli enjoyed from the bus
what made valli laugh until tears came

solution_steps.explain: The canal, palm trees, mountains and green fields delighted Valli, and the galloping cow made her laugh.
The bus conductor spoke with practiced joviality and addressed her as madam.
She stayed on the bus at the town stop because she wanted the return trip on the same bus.

concepts.title: The Dead Cow and the Mystery of Life and Death
concepts.definition: On the return journey Valli sees the same cow lying dead by the roadside where a fast-moving vehicle had struck it, and the sight drains all her laughter, giving her a first glimpse of death.
concepts.key_idea: Valli no longer wants to look out of the window; the memory of the dead cow haunts her, and she reaches home thoughtful, aware of the gap between knowing about death and understanding it.
question_patterns: why didn't valli want to go to the stall and have a drink
what did valli see on the return journey that upset her
how did the sight of the dead cow change valli
what does the story tell us about the mystery of life and death
why was valli no longer interested in the window sights
how did valli behave after reaching home

solution_steps.explain: The cow that had galloped before the bus now lay dead by the roadside.
Laughter turns to sadness; she refuses the drink and stops looking out of the window.
The episode introduces the mystery of life and death, which the introduction calls her induction into the world outside her village.
